title: Arkret High-Risk Authority Proof Family
description: Shared authority proof family for service operations that key-management.md designates as high-risk material destruction or equivalent (first consumer: active-series key backup tail deletion, key-management.md section 7.8). Exactly one closed branch: principal_signing, device_quorum, or trusted_recovery_service, discriminated by `kind`. Every branch reuses the common detached-JWS leaf (event-envelope.schema.json#/$defs/proof) over the operation's single canonical delete-intent transcript; branches never restate the leaf fields. An ordinary current-device session proof is deliberately NOT a branch of this family — operations that accept it for low-risk paths must say so in their own normative text. cross-signing-reset.schema.json keeps its own raw-signature proof shapes because its section 14.1 transcript embeds proof_body material inside the signed bytes; the branch taxonomy (kind names and verification obligations) is aligned with this family, the signature leaf is not, and no third hand-copied definition may be introduced.

detached_proof.description: Common detached-JWS leaf. `payload_digest` MUST be the digest of the operation's canonical transcript (for key backup deletion: the delete-intent transcript of key-management.md section 7.8.1); `created_at` MUST fall inside the server-issued challenge window when the operation binds one.

principal_signing_proof.description: Principal-control-key proof. The proof's verification_method MUST be a principal-grade DID-control verification method whose controller DID is byte-identical to the transcript's principal_id, and that key MUST be a currently accepted principal control key at proof.created_at. Device keys, service keys and retired keys MUST be rejected.

proof.description: Detached-JWS leaf whose verification_method MUST resolve, at proof.created_at, to an authorized non-revoked device key of exactly this device_id under the transcript's principal_id. Every quorum member signs the same canonical transcript bytes.

device_quorum_proof.description: Device-quorum proof. The schema enforces only the minimum wire shape (threshold>=2, signatures.minItems=1). Verification is normative in the consuming operation's text: (a) every signature MUST verify over the same canonical transcript; (b) signatures MUST be deduplicated by device_id; (c) the count of valid deduplicated signatures MUST be >= threshold; (d) threshold MUST equal the currently accepted recovery policy device-quorum k — a smaller issuer-supplied threshold MUST be rejected as failed_precondition. A deployment whose policy k is below 2 cannot use this branch and must use principal_signing or trusted_recovery_service instead; a single current device proof is not a high-risk quorum.

threshold.description: The quorum threshold the issuer claims to satisfy. MUST equal the principal's currently accepted recovery_policy device-quorum k; receivers MUST cross-check per description rule (d).

signatures.description: minItems=1 is the schema floor only; receiver-side verification requires deduplicated valid signature count >= threshold per description rule (c).

trusted_recovery_service_proof.description: Trusted recovery service proof. The verification_method of `proof` MUST be controlled by service_id, and service_id MUST be authorized as a trusted recovery service by the recovery policy / DID delegation snapshotted into the referenced recovery session. The session MUST be unexpired, unconsumed for this purpose, and MUST have been established by principal_signing, recovery unlock or device_quorum — the service alone is never a sufficient factor.

recovery_session_id.description: Verified, unexpired, unconsumed recovery session authenticated by principal_signing, recovery unlock or device_quorum. A service-only session is not a second factor.

attestation_ref.description: Optional attestation object for service_id. If present, receivers MUST resolve it in the same trust_domain as the operation and reject cross-domain attestations.
